name: Gradient Boosting
learningObjectives: Understand the gradient boosting ensemble method and sequential learning
Learn how weak learners (decision stumps) are combined to create strong predictors
Explore the role of learning rate in controlling overfitting
Understand residual-based training and gradient descent in function space
Compare gradient boosting with other ensemble methods like Random Forest

controls.label: Dataset
controls.tooltip: Choose a classification dataset to train on

controls.label: Number of Estimators
controls.tooltip: Number of weak learners (decision stumps) in the ensemble. More estimators can improve performance but may cause overfitting.

controls.label: Learning Rate
controls.tooltip: Controls the contribution of each weak learner. Lower values require more estimators but can improve generalization.

controls.label: Max Depth
controls.tooltip: Maximum depth of each decision stump. Deeper stumps can capture more complex patterns but may overfit.

controls.label: Min Samples Split
controls.tooltip: Minimum number of samples required to split an internal node. Higher values prevent overfitting.

controls.label: Subsample Ratio
controls.tooltip: Fraction of samples used for training each weak learner. Values < 1.0 introduce stochasticity and can improve generalization.
